style.name: K1-minimal · house look (locked 2026-10-15)
style.block: A 2D key frame from a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light and the place: a warm, soft key light from the upper left that falls in soft, hazy beams; a real place behind the figures, built of simple flat paper planes with no ink outline, each plane further back paler and softer in a warm haze, so depth comes from haze and never from blur; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; soft violet cast shadows on the walls and the floor, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.
style.world: In Its Order, episode 01 of The Path of the Just, a narrated explainer film about growing in Christ in God's order: milk first, then meat, and the meat is more of Christ. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky, a real place in a soft haze. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE BEAT'S BRIEF (the words in «» are what the narrator says as each change lands): STORY: a cardboard courtyard at a village wedding, teal day, lanterns strung, a long table of bread, fruit and dishes. On «A baby drinks milk, and nobody…» a mother lifts a cup to a baby's lips, close on the baby's glad face. On «But picture a young man at…» the camera trucks down the table to a tall young man in his festive long cream tunic and teal mantle, the series lead; on «still asking for his bottle.» he holds up a baby's bottle, hopeful, and the guests either side turn and stare (a light moment). On «Now picture a letter to believers…» a rolled scroll drops onto the table in front of him and unrolls; on «They are become such as have…» its words are not shown (CRAFT rule 1), only the gold seal. On «And that letter is in our…» he winces. On «So what is milk, and what…» the camera lifts to a cup of milk and a platter of bread side by side, the only props lit. The narration's words appear only as full-screen cards: nothing in the picture carries lettering.

THE MOMENT: this frame holds from the narrator's words «A baby drinks milk, and nobody…»: draw what the brief has on screen at that moment, and nothing the brief brings in later.

One clean, calm, finished 16:9 animated-film frame: not a photograph, not a comic page, not a character sheet, no panels or borders.

The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE ACT: "feast": a bright, high-key frame, with rich, warm colour.

THE BEAT'S BRIEF (the words in «» are what the narrator says as each change lands): IDEA: the parchment page, matched from the cup on the courtyard table in cold. A grown linen villager holds a small clay cup; on «As newborn babes, desire the sincere…» a book opens beside it and a ribbon of white pours from its pages into the cup («So the milk is God's word,…»). On «with nothing mixed in.» a dropper of dark ink hovers over the cup and is waved away. On «A baby cannot do without it.» the cup passes along a row of linen villagers of every height (the baby, the toddler, the child, the grown villager), each drinking in turn; on «and there is no shame in…» the series lead from cold, in his cream tunic and teal mantle, takes a cup too and smiles. The narration's words appear only as full-screen cards: nothing in the picture carries lettering.

Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE ACT: "foundation": a mid-key frame, neither bright nor dark, with gently saturated colour.

The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light and the place: a warm, soft key light from the upper left that falls in soft, hazy beams; a real place behind the figures, built of simple flat paper planes with no ink outline, each plane further back paler and softer in a warm haze, so depth comes from haze and never from blur; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; soft violet cast shadows on the walls and the floor, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

The first reference image shows the art style only: take its line, shapes, colour handling, faces, paper texture and light, but none of its people, its room or its layout. Its hands float free beside the body, which this film no longer draws: every hand here is at the end of an arm in its sleeve.

THE FILM'S WORLD: In Its Order, episode 01 of The Path of the Just, a narrated explainer film about growing in Christ in God's order: milk first, then meat, and the meat is more of Christ. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky, a real place in a soft haze. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE ACT: "growing": a bright, high-key frame, with rich, warm colour.

THE BEAT'S BRIEF (the words in «» are what the narrator says as each change lands): IDEA: the series map. The parchment widens into a long hill: the six stones at its foot (Tier One), the gold path climbing past a veil, a small tent sanctuary, two tablets in an ark and a resting figure under a tree (Tier Two), up to a city on the summit under a dawn sky (Tier Three). On «The path of the just is…» the dawn behind the summit brightens in three soft steps, more and more, never all at once. On «And all of it is Christ.» the gold cross's light from «a priest in heaven,» spreads until the whole hill lies inside it. The narration's words appear only as full-screen cards: nothing in the picture carries lettering.

THE FILM'S WORLD: In Its Order, episode 01 of The Path of the Just, a narrated explainer film about growing in Christ in God's order: milk first, then meat, and the meat is more of Christ. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky, a real place in a soft haze. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE ACT: "growing": a bright, high-key frame, with rich, warm colour.

THE BEAT'S BRIEF (the words in «» are what the narrator says as each change lands): IDEA and STORY merged, the landing: the wedding courtyard from cold in the same layout and framing, now under the teal-to-yellow landing sky. The series lead stands where he stood; on «The young man sets down his…» he sets the baby's bottle down. On «But because the table was set…» the host's hand (the host is Christ, in the seamless linen coat and the walnut mantle, at the head of the table) gestures to the place set for him: bread from the field in grain, and on «and the milk is on it…» the cup of milk from milk beside the plate. On «O taste and see that the…» he tastes, close on his face, delight. On «Going from milk to meat never…» the six stones show for a breath as the courtyard's paving under the table. On «It is growing up into him.» he stands taller beside the host; the gold cross's light from priest warms the whole courtyard. The held pause comes after «It is growing up into him.». The narration's words appear only as full-screen cards: nothing in the picture carries lettering.

A 2D key frame from a narrated animated film, drawn in this art style: our own K1 paper-cut look made minimal, the house look, as the reference image shows it. Every figure and prop is a few flat cut-paper shapes. Every figure and prop has a thick warm dark-brown ink outline and a thin light inner edge just inside it, and is creased once by a single straight diagonal line at the light's angle, its far side a deeper hue of its own colour turned toward violet, never grey and never black. A head is ONE simple shape inside one single thick outline, and the light inner edge runs round that one outline. Garments are flat planes: no pockets, no buttons, no stitching, no seams, no cuffs, no fabric texture. Hands are plain round paper circles at the end of each arm in its sleeve, the sleeve running from the shoulder to the hand: never a hand floating free of the body, never a bare arm, no thumbs, no fingers. Faces are three marks only: two small dark ink oval eyes, short brows and a one-line mouth. One muted hue per piece. The light and the place: a warm, soft key light from the upper left that falls in soft, hazy beams; a real place behind the figures, built of simple flat paper planes with no ink outline, each plane further back paler and softer in a warm haze, so depth comes from haze and never from blur; a soft paper grain on every piece and every plane; soft violet cast shadows on the walls and the floor, never a darker brown; a muted, warm palette in which only the film's accents are loud. Keep it K1: no white sticker border round the figures, no felt or stitching style, no big glossy eyes, no realistic anatomy. The look is stylised, attractive, expressive and minimal.

The first reference image shows the art style only: take its line, shapes, colour handling, faces, paper texture and light, but none of its people, its room or its layout. Its hands float free beside the body, which this film no longer draws: every hand here is at the end of an arm in its sleeve.

THE FILM'S WORLD: In Its Order, episode 01 of The Path of the Just, a narrated explainer film about growing in Christ in God's order: milk first, then meat, and the meat is more of Christ. It has two registers: an IDEA beat is a light parchment page with figures and props cut from paper laid on it; a STORY beat is a cardboard diorama of three to five layered paper planes under a simple two- or three-stop gradient sky, a real place in a soft haze. Its places: a village wedding feast in a chipboard courtyard under a teal day sky, lanterns strung over a long table of bread, fruit, cups and dishes, guests seated along it; the six paper stones of the foundation on the parchment, each with a small gold icon, and a gold path running on from the last of them; the holy place, where a tall veil of fine linen woven with blue, purple and scarlet (Exodus 26:31: a muted priest blue, a sanctuary purple and the muted cloth crimson) glows gold from behind; a field on a hillside under a peach morning, a low stone wall near; a Corinthian room at dusk, the film's one short valley; a small lamplit room in Jerusalem; and a small cardboard hill with an empty cross at dawn. The landing returns to the same courtyard, in the same layout, under a sky going from teal to yellow. Everyone in the film is drawn on the cast canon, about 3.36 heads tall, and each named person exactly as their references draw them. The plain figures of the IDEA page are grey paper or undyed linen, of every height. The Bible's people wear the story cloth: linen, walnut, indigo, olive and camel, of varied heights, builds and headcloths, never clones. Jesus is an ordinary Jewish man with no halo: on earth in a seamless linen coat and a walnut mantle; as Priest in a white robe with a golden girdle and the breastplate. The colour script is bright, with no black moment: teal day at the feast, peach on the parchment, dawn coming in on the page, dawn gold behind the veil, teal going to yellow at the landing. White only for the milk and the priest's robe; gold only for God's word and the light from the cross, and only gold glows; no bright scarlet anywhere: the veil's red is the muted cloth crimson of its thread, never glowing; everything else calm creams, chipboard browns, taupes, teals and peaches. No lettering in any picture: the narration's words are full-screen cards.

THE ACT: "growing": a bright, high-key frame, with rich, warm colour.
